chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

A man came to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, inform me about noble character (makarim al-akhlaq). He said: Forgiving those who wrong you, maintaining ties with those who cut you off, giving to those who deprive you, and speaking the truth even if it be against yourself.

key_terms.الحق: The truth/right — speaking honestly regardless of personal consequence
key_terms.العفو: Pardon/forgiveness — the disposition to overlook wrongs done by others
key_terms.صلة: Maintaining ties — specifically reconnecting with those who have severed the relationship
key_terms.مكارم الأخلاق: Noble character traits — the highest expressions of moral virtue in Islamic ethics

ai.seo_question: What are the traits of noble character (makarim al-akhlaq) according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked by a man to describe noble character (makarim al-akhlaq). The Imam enumerated four defining virtues: pardoning those who oppress you, reconnecting with those who sever ties, being generous to those who withhold from you, and always speaking the truth even at personal cost. This teaching, transmitted through a chain of highly trustworthy Shia narrators, encapsulates the Imam's emphasis on a moral life that transcends transactional reciprocity.
